newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Eravis pays no dividend but invests.
newsitem.headline: Eravis pays no dividend but invests.

text.p: Hungarian hotel group Eravis Rt will not pay dividend on its 14.9 million forints 1996 net profit but will go on with its investments following shareholders approval on Thursday.
Eravis, which operates hotels up to three stars, as well as students and workers' hostels, did not pay dividend last year either.

The group in which large-scale restructuring has been underway with around 1.5 billion forints of investments in the last three years, will continue the modernisation which has already resulted in a higher market share, Eravis CEO Gyorgy Karikas told shareholders.
"We managed to strengthen our market share," Karikas said. "Our figures justify that we are able to maintain our competitive edge."

This year's business plan calls for the investment of 700 million forints, of which 150 million was an interest-free loan provided by the Ministry of Industry, Trade and Tourism, 337 million was a commercial loan provided under favourable conditions while the rest comes from own sources.
On operating level Eravis has improved and boosted its operating profit to 233.3 million forints in 1996 from 194.0 million in 1995.

The company surpassed its 210 million forint operating profit target of 1996, but its investments including the acquisition of a 50 percent stake in Hunguest hotel chain, lowered its after-tax profit to 14.9 million from 200.4 million in 1995.
The group's 1997 business plan sees an operating profit of 270 million and Karikas said the first quarter was encouraging.
"We fulfilled the first quarter in line with plans," Karikas said, without giving figures.

Answering complaints of small shareholders who had bought their shares in 1995 for a mixture of cash and compensation coupons and complained of not receiving dividend and not having opportunities to lock in profits from share price increases due to low share price, the company said it will continue a share buy-back.

"The company would like to continue share buy-backs from next week on," Deputy General Director responsible for finances, Istvan Hulvely said, adding Hungary's new securities act was forbidding share buy-backs before the general meetings.

Hulvely said the company bought back shares worth around a nominal 50 million forints last year and expected to buy back a similar amount this year. He said he estimated small shareholders having some 300 million forints of nominal shares.
Eravis shares have a 10,000 forint face value but have always traded below that. On Thursday Eravis shares closed at 4,300 forints, unchanged from Wednesday.
